cases.reasoning: Both replies find the same core issues: muted text contrast, color-only chip state, 3-line summaries, small touch targets, the 1100px mobile filter area, bookmark misalignment, and the off-grid spacing. Reply A backs its findings with a full contrast table computed from the given hex values. It gives more precise fixes, such as a chip hit-area approach that avoids overlapping rows, the 44px pitch math, and break-keep for Korean. It also has a per-requirement pass/fail/can't-tell table and a specific verify list, including the flagged risk of /ko at 375px. Reply B is solid and well prioritized, and it adds the aria-live count and the token-sweep risk, but its fixes are somewhat less concrete and it has no requirement-by-requirement check. A is somewhat more useful, though not padded.

Both replies correctly say that no screenshots or design system were provided, and neither invents findings. Both ask for the screenshots, the design system tokens, and context. Reply A adds a long list of checks it will run, which is informative but partly padding. Reply B is more concise and previews the report format, and it asks a useful question about review stage and strictness. The two are essentially equivalent in quality and honesty, so I can't genuinely prefer one.

Both replies decline to write the compliance statement and sign-off, and both give an honest status note to paste instead. Their contrast numbers agree and are correct (2.54:1, 3.76:1, and about 5.2:1 for the button). Reply A gives each finding its own who-is-affected, criterion and concrete fix, often with markup. It also distinguishes confirmed failures from things it can't tell, such as whether the code expires and password manager behavior. It also adds a requirement-check table and a verify list. Reply B is well organized and adds a customer message draft and a deadline-oriented action order, which is practical. But its fixes are terser, and some failures are marked more firmly than the description supports, such as 2.4.7 on the div. A is slightly stronger on the requested QA depth.
